payload.title: isPointInTimeRecord reads the Status header from raw lines with no fence mask, so a Status: Proposed or Draft line inside a code block in the first 40 lines turns a live document into a record and silences all of its references
evidence: tools/aria-adapters/doc-staleness-adapter.ts:184-196 (fenceMask exists in the same file and is used by the reference roles)
tools/aria-adapters/doc-staleness-adapter.ts:375-378 (STATUS_HEADER_RES match any line that spells a status, with no notion of a fence or a blockquote)
tools/aria-adapters/doc-staleness-adapter.ts:405 (the status test slices the first 40 raw lines and never consults a fence mask)
tools/aria-adapters/doc-staleness-adapter.test.ts:448-466 (the window scenario pins lines 40, 41 and 80 but holds no case for a fenced Status line)
payload.rule_violated: DOCROLES SPEC ruling 1 (the document's own header states its status) and the adapter's own convention that fenced lines are code, not prose (referenceRole already masks them).
payload.notes: A guide that teaches how to write an ADR and shows the template in a code block with a Status: Proposed line within its first 40 lines is read as a record: calling isPointInTimeRecord on such a document returned true at a81bfa2d6 (probe with the template block and a later reference to a missing apps path). Every stale reference of that guide then goes unreported. Not reachable on the current tree: none of the 32 documents with a Status line in their first 40 lines has it inside a fence, and no fenced status line exists anywhere under the scan roots. Close condition: Apply fenceMask(lines) to the status check (and to the header marker test beside it) and add a case to semantic-status-header-records plus a unit scenario in which a fenced Status: Proposed keeps the document live and its missing path flagged. Verified at origin/main a81bfa2d6.
